html:
The Hungarian Revolution of 1848 was a rising for reform and independence that began in Pest on 15 March 1848, part of the revolutions of 1848, and became a war against Austria until its defeat in 1849.

The poet Sándor Petőfi read his National Song to the crowds, and the Habsburgs accepted the April Laws, which ended serfdom and gave Hungary its own government. When Vienna turned against it, Lajos Kossuth led a war of independence. In April 1849 Hungary declared the Habsburgs deposed. Russia's Tsar Nicholas I sent some 200,000 troops to help Austria, and the Hungarians surrendered at Világos in August. On 6 October thirteen generals were executed at Arad. 15 March is a national day in Hungary, and the Compromise of 1867 later gave back much of what was lost.
